# missBART

Joint models for multivariate responses with non-ignorable missing
values, built on Bayesian additive regression trees (BART).

The responses follow a multivariate BART model. The missingness
indicators follow a model in which the responses themselves are
predictors, so that data missing completely at random, missing at random
and missing not at random (MNAR) can all be handled, and the missing
responses are imputed while the model is fitted:

| Function | Model for the missingness |
|----|----|
| [`missBART1()`](reference/missBART.md) | multivariate probit regression on `(1, x, y)` |
| [`missBART2()`](reference/missBART.md) | multivariate probit BART on `(x, y)` |
| [`mvBART()`](reference/mvBART.md) | none: multivariate BART for complete responses |

The methods are described in

> Goh, Y. C., Soh, W. K., Parnell, A. C. and Murphy, K. (2024). Joint
> models for handling non-ignorable missing data using Bayesian additive
> regression trees: application to leaf photosynthetic traits data.
> [arXiv:2412.14946](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14946)

## Installation

The samplers are written in C++ (Rcpp and RcppArmadillo), so a C++
toolchain is needed to install from source (Rtools on Windows, Xcode
command line tools on macOS).

``` r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("yongchengoh/missBART")
```

## Example

``` r
library(missBART)

set.seed(1)
n <- 500
x <- matrix(runif(n * 5), ncol = 5)
y_true <- cbind(10 * sin(pi * x[, 1] * x[, 2]) + 10 * x[, 4], 5 * x[, 1] - 8 * x[, 2]^2) +
  matrix(rnorm(2 * n), ncol = 2)

# large values are more likely to be missing
y <- y_true
y[runif(n) < pnorm(-1 + scale(y_true[, 1])), 1] <- NA
y[runif(n) < pnorm(-1 + scale(y_true[, 2])), 2] <- NA

fit1 <- missBART1(x, y)                      # probit regression missingness model
fit2 <- missBART2(x, y, n_class_trees = 20)  # probit BART missingness model

fit1
head(imputed_values(fit1))   # posterior summaries of the missing responses
y_complete <- completed_data(fit1)
coef(fit1)                   # probit coefficients: is the missingness driven by y?
varimp(fit2)                 # which predictors the missingness trees split on
```

[`vignette("missBART")`](articles/missBART.md) has a longer
walk-through, and the package website (built into `docs/`) has further
articles, including a re-run of the simulation studies in the paper.
Scripts for the simulations and the application in the paper are in
[`Examples/`](Examples).

## Speed

Version 0.2.0 moved the samplers from R to C++. Seconds per 1,000 MCMC
iterations on simulated MNAR data with five covariates, 100 regression
trees and (for `missBART2`) 20 missingness trees, single core:

| n    | responses | model     | 0.1.0 (R) | 0.2.0 (C++) | speed-up |
|------|-----------|-----------|----------:|------------:|---------:|
| 500  | 1         | missBART1 |        95 |        0.57 |     170x |
| 500  | 1         | missBART2 |       110 |        0.63 |     170x |
| 500  | 1         | mvBART    |        86 |        0.48 |     180x |
| 2000 | 2         | missBART1 |      1043 |         3.0 |     350x |
| 2000 | 2         | missBART2 |       248 |         2.9 |      90x |
| 2000 | 2         | mvBART    |       186 |         2.1 |      90x |
| 2000 | 5         | missBART1 |      1553 |         5.4 |     290x |
| 2000 | 5         | missBART2 |       389 |         5.0 |      80x |
| 2000 | 5         | mvBART    |       304 |         3.5 |      90x |

The C++ timings are averages over 5,000 iterations. The R timings are
averages over the first 50 iterations only, when the trees are still
small, so they flatter the R code. At these rates the 10,000 iterations
used in the paper for `n = 2000` and five responses take about 55
seconds with `missBART1`, instead of about 4.3 hours.
[`Examples/benchmark.R`](Examples/benchmark.R) reproduces the table.

Running both versions for the same 2,000 iterations on one simulated
data set (`n = 500`, two responses) gave:

| model     | time 0.1.0 | time 0.2.0 | imputation RMSE 0.1.0 | imputation RMSE 0.2.0 |
|-----------|-----------:|-----------:|----------------------:|----------------------:|
| missBART1 |      621 s |      2.0 s |                  1.24 |                  1.15 |
| missBART2 |      246 s |      1.8 s |                  1.16 |                  1.15 |
| mvBART    |      196 s |      1.1 s |                     – |                     – |

The two versions do not produce identical draws for the same seed, and a
few steps of the sampler were changed; see [`NEWS.md`](NEWS.md).

# Package index

## Models

Fit the joint models, or multivariate BART on its own.

- [`missBART1()`](missBART.md) [`missBARTprobit()`](missBART.md)
  [`missBART2()`](missBART.md) : Joint BART models for responses with
  non-ignorable missingness
- [`mvBART()`](mvBART.md) : Multivariate BART for complete responses

## Summarising a fit

- [`print(`*`<missBART>`*`)`](missBART-methods.md)
  [`summary(`*`<missBART>`*`)`](missBART-methods.md)
  [`fitted(`*`<missBART>`*`)`](missBART-methods.md)
  [`predict(`*`<missBART>`*`)`](missBART-methods.md)
  [`coef(`*`<missBART>`*`)`](missBART-methods.md) : Methods for missBART
  fits
- [`imputed_values()`](imputed_values.md)
  [`completed_data()`](imputed_values.md) : Summaries of the imputed
  responses
- [`varimp()`](varimp.md) : Variable importance

## Priors and settings

- [`hypers_list()`](hypers_list.md) : BART prior parameters
- [`tree_list()`](tree_list.md) : Tree prior parameters
- [`probit_prior_list()`](probit_prior_list.md) : Prior for the probit
  regression coefficients of missBART1

## Simulating data

- [`sim_data_friedman()`](sim_data_friedman.md) : Simulate
- [`sim_data_trees()`](sim_data_trees.md) : Simulating data from trees
- [`sim_missing_probit()`](sim_missing_probit.md) : Simulating missing
  values from a probit regression model
- [`sim_missing_trees()`](sim_missing_trees.md) : Simulate missing data
  from a BART model
- [`propose_tree()`](propose_tree.md) : A function for proposing an
  updated tree structure

## Utilities

- [`scale_bart()`](scale_bart.md) [`unscale()`](scale_bart.md) : Scaling
  responses to and from the BART scale
- [`rMVN()`](rMVN.md) : Sampling once from a multivariate normal
  distribution with mean mu and precision Q
- [`rMVNc()`](rMVNc.md) : Sampling from a multivariate normal
  distribution with precision Q and mean equal to the solution of Q mu =
  b
- [`multi_rMVN()`](multi_rMVN.md) : Sampling multiple times from a
  multivariate normal distribution
- [`matrnorm()`](matrnorm.md) : Sampling from a matrix normal
  distribution MV(mu, U, V)
- [`missBART-package`](missBART-package.md) : missBART: joint models for
  non-ignorable missing responses using BART
